title: Shopping for food (Einkaufen)
summary: Buy food at the market, the bakery and the supermarket: ask for an amount, ask what it costs, and pay.
goals: Ask for an amount: ein Kilo, zweihundert Gramm, eine Flasche
Ask what something costs and understand the price
Answer Sonst noch etwas? and pay, in cash or by card

nicosWeg.title: Nicos Weg A1, chapter 12: Food (Mengen und Preise, Was darf es sein?, Sonst noch etwas?)

points: Words: [[der Supermarkt]], [[die Einkaufsliste]] (shopping list), [[der Einkaufswagen]] (trolley), [[der Einkaufskorb]] (basket), [[die Abteilung]] (section), [[die Kasse]] (checkout), [[der Kassierer]], [[die Kassiererin]], [[der Kunde]], [[die Kundin]], [[der Kassenbon]] or [[der Kassenzettel]] (receipt).
Going, being, coming back: [[Ich gehe zum Supermarkt.]], [[Ich bin im Supermarkt.]], [[Ich komme vom Supermarkt.]]
Buying: amount + product, no 'of', and the accusative for masculine words: [[Ich kaufe eine Dose Cola.]], [[Ich möchte einen Becher Joghurt und eine Tafel Schokolade.]]
Weights and volumes: [[das Kilo]], [[ein halbes Kilo]] (500 g), [[das Gramm]], [[das Pfund]] (500 g, less common); [[der Liter]], [[ein halber Liter]].

Can't find something? [[Entschuldigen Sie, wo finde ich hier Chips?]] - [[Chips finden Sie beim Knabberzeug.]] Other sections: [[bei den Getränken]], [[bei Obst und Gemüse]], [[bei der Tiefkühlkost]] (frozen food), [[bei den Backwaren]].
At the checkout: [[Das macht 25,10 Euro.]] - [[Bitte.]] When you leave: [[Einen schönen Tag!]] - [[Danke, ebenso.]] (you too)

phrases.de: Ich möchte ein Stück Käse kaufen.
phrases.en: I'd like to buy a piece of cheese.
I'm buying a packet of washing powder.
I'm buying a bottle of oil.
I'd like a jar of honey.

phrases.de: Ich möchte ein halbes Kilo Äpfel.
phrases.en: I'd like half a kilo of apples.
I'm buying a litre of milk.

phrases.de: Entschuldigen Sie, wo finde ich hier Chips?
phrases.en: Excuse me, where can I find crisps here?
That's 25.10 euros.
Have a nice day! Thanks, you too.

points: [[die Verpackung]] means packaging. Each type goes with typical products, with no 'of' between them: [[eine Dose Cola]].
[[die Dose]] (can), [[die Flasche]] (bottle), [[das Glas]] (jar), [[die Tube]] (tube), [[der Becher]] (pot, tub), [[die Packung]] (packet, carton), [[die Tafel]] (bar, of chocolate).
[[der Beutel]] (bag, of rice or coffee), [[die Tüte]] (paper or plastic bag, of sweets or flour), [[das Netz]] (net, of onions or oranges), [[die Schale]] (punnet, of strawberries).
[[der Kasten]] (crate, of beer or water), [[die Schachtel]] (box, of chocolates), [[der Sechserpack]] (six-pack).
In a sentence, masculine packaging takes the accusative: [[Ich möchte einen Beutel Reis kaufen.]]
Supermarket flyers ([[der Prospekt]]) show the offers ([[das Angebot]]) with the packaging: good reading practice.

phrases.en: a can of tomatoes
a bottle of water
a jar of jam
a tube of toothpaste
a pot of yoghurt
a packet of pasta
a crate of water
a punnet of strawberries

phrases.de: Ich möchte einen Beutel Reis kaufen.
phrases.en: I'd like to buy a bag of rice.

notes.extra: About 15 kinds of packaging, with products for each.

points: Germany's big supermarket chains include Lidl, Aldi, Rewe, Netto, Edeka, Penny and Kaufland.
Tip 1: you need a coin for the trolley: [[Du brauchst eine Münze für den Einkaufswagen.]]

Sections: [[Obst und Gemüse]], [[Milchprodukte]], [[Backwaren]] (bread), [[Fleisch und Wurst]], [[Tiefkühlprodukte]] (frozen), [[Getränke]], [[Haushaltswaren]], [[Süßwaren]] (sweets), [[Fertiggerichte]] (ready meals).
Useful words: [[das Sonderangebot]] (special offer), [[der Kassenzettel]] or [[der Bon]] (receipt), [[bar oder mit Karte zahlen]], [[das Leergut]] (empty bottles to return).
Tip 2: don't hesitate to ask. Start with [[Entschuldigen Sie bitte]], then your question.
At the checkout you pack your bags yourself, and you may be asked: [[Sammeln Sie Punkte?]] (loyalty points), [[Bar oder Karte?]], [[Möchten Sie eine Tüte?]] (bags cost extra).

phrases.en: Where can I find the bread?

phrases.de: Das Brot ist dort hinten neben dem Käse.
phrases.en: The bread is back there next to the cheese.

phrases.de: Haben Sie auch Wasser ohne Kohlensäure?
phrases.en: Do you also have still water?

phrases.en: Come with me, I'll show you.

phrases.de: Der Zucker ist im dritten Gang neben dem Mehl.

Can I pay by card?

phrases.de: Wie möchten Sie zahlen? Bar oder Karte?

Would you like a bag?
That's 18.60 euros altogether.

notes.extra: Supermarket habits: a coin for the trolley, packing your own bags, loyalty points, [[Leergut]], and [[Wasser ohne Kohlensäure]] (still water).

points: Hundreds and thousands are the number plus [[hundert]] or [[tausend]]: [[zweihundert]], [[sechshundert]], [[dreitausend]]. 100 is [[hundert]] or [[einhundert]].
A number is one word, however long: 634 is [[sechshundertvierunddreißig]] (hundreds, then ones, then tens).
Germans group thousands with a point, not a comma: 11.000 is [[elftausend]]. The comma is the decimal mark: 2,50 €.
Big numbers: [[hunderttausend]], [[eine Million]], plural [[zwei Millionen]]; [[eine Milliarde]], plural [[zwei Milliarden]]. Careful: [[Milliarde]] is an English billion.
Years up to 1999 are said in hundreds: 1995 is [[neunzehnhundertfünfundneunzig]]. From 2000 they are normal numbers: 2017 is [[zweitausendsiebzehn]].
Your year of birth: [[Ich bin neunzehnhundertneunzig geboren.]] or [[im Jahr 1990]], never 'in 1990'.

phrases.en: one million, two million
1995 (as a year)
I was born in 1990.

sections.text: As with [[ein Glas Wasser]] in lesson 1, there's no 'of'. Masculine and neuter measures don't take a plural ending after a number: [[zwei Kilo]], [[drei Liter]], [[zwei Stück Kuchen]], and prices: [[zehn Euro]]. Feminine ones do: [[zwei Flaschen Wasser]], [[zwei Tassen Tee]].

sections.title: Prices
sections.text:
[[Was kostet das?]] or [[Wie viel kostet das?]] = How much is it? For more than one thing: [[Was kosten die Äpfel?]]

Prices are said like this:
- 2,50 € = [[zwei Euro fünfzig]]
- 12,90 € = [[zwölf Euro neunzig]]
- 0,99 € = [[neunundneunzig Cent]]

You practised the numbers in Unit 0. Germans write a comma in prices: 2,50 €, not 2.50.

sections.title: At the counter
sections.text:
- [[Was darf es sein?]] = What can I get you? (A fixed phrase; [[darf]] comes in Unit 5.)
- [[Ich hätte gern ...]] or [[Ich nehme ...]]
- [[Sonst noch etwas?]] = Anything else?
- [[Nein, danke. Das ist alles.]] = No thanks, that's all.
- [[Das macht sechs Euro achtzig.]] = That comes to 6.80 euros.
- [[Bar oder mit Karte?]] = Cash or card? - [[Mit Karte, bitte.]] or [[Bar.]] ([[mit Karte]] is a chunk; Unit 6 explains [[mit]].)

In a supermarket you pay at [[die Kasse]] (the checkout).

sections.title: Cash
sections.text: Germans still like cash. Most shops take cards, but some small bakeries and market stalls take only cash. If you're not sure, ask: [[Kann ich mit Karte zahlen?]]

items.de: Guten Tag! Was darf es sein?
items.en: Hello! What can I get you?

items.de: Ich hätte gern ein Kilo Tomaten.
items.en: I'd like a kilo of tomatoes.

items.de: Ja, zweihundert Gramm Käse, bitte. Was kostet das?
items.en: Yes, 200 grams of cheese, please. How much is that?

items.question: How much is it?
items.explanation: vier Euro fünfzig = 4,50 €: euros first, then the cents.

items.instruction: Fill in the gap: How much are the apples?
items.explanation: die Äpfel is plural, so kosten. One thing: Was kostet der Apfel?

items.question: The seller asks 'Sonst noch etwas?'. You have everything. What do you say?
items.explanation: Sonst noch etwas? = Anything else? Das ist alles = that's all.
ein Kilo Äpfel: the amount, then the food, with no 'of'.
kann in first place (a yes/no question), zahlen or bezahlen at the end.
